text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- PLO leader Yasser Arafat is expected to visit Finland next week, but it is uncertain whether he will.
- Candidates who supported Finland's membership in the EU got more votes in last week's EU elections than those against.
- Ministry of education's international exchange department to organise voluntary work abroad for unemployed youth. @
- Finnish forests are growing satisfactorily, little affected by air pollutants, says forestry research institute.
- Finnish cardbox recycling business coming under pressure from international competitors. Biggest purchaser Corenso shifts attention to Sweden where cardbox recycling gets state support.
- Government to decide next week on cutting milk production quotas.
- Finnish exporters have reduced their hedging of currency flows after the markka's linked to ERM. @
- Despite the growth in cd-rom popularity, Finnish production is a loss-making business due to heavy production costs and small market size.
- Changes in angling license regulation generate lively debate in parliament.
- Finnish municipalities want to transfer administration of income support scheme to national social security system.
- Finland and EU have still not reached agreement on alcohol regulation policy, but differences between them are narrowing. @
- Finland will lose the option of joining Nato if it is excluded from the first round of enlargement, says Tapani Vaahtoranta of the Foreign policy research institute.
